text: The Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction, an oscillating chemical system, can literally solve maze problems: chemical wavefronts propagating from the entrance reach the exit fastest along the shortest path.
explanation: True. In the BZ excitable medium, waves obey pass/block/annihilate collision rules (like neural refractoriness), and when a maze is filled with BZ solution the wavefront traveling the shortest route arrives first, reading out the answer (Steinbock, Toth and Showalter, 1995). This is genuine computation performed by chemistry, not a metaphor, though it is slow and hard to program.
